headline: Amazon has announced three Android tablets with its Alexa+ assistant and Google Play access, but the assistant needs a Prime or separate subscription and the lower-priced models show lock-screen ads unless owners pay $20.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a mainstream consumer launch with real-world limits, but a hardware refresh rather than a new AI capability.
importance_line: Shoppers in the US, Canada, Mexico and five European countries can buy the tablets from 14 or 19 Oct, but the AI assistant costs extra unless they already have Prime and ads can be removed only for a fee.
summary: Business Today reports that Amazon has introduced three Android tablets, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, 11 and 8, plus Kids versions, that run Google Play apps and its Alexa+ assistant, priced from $229.99 to $549.99 and shipping from 14 Oct in the US, Mexico and Canada. The catch is that Alexa+ needs an Amazon Prime membership or a separate subscription, and removing lock-screen ads costs a one-time $20 on eligible models.
notes: Announcement date not stated; published 9 Oct 2026.
